mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route if the receiving state is an Apostille Convention member: MOEA issuance -> notarization before a Taiwan notary public -> Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular Legalization route if the receiving state is a non-member: MOEA issuance -> notarization -> MOEA authentication -> legalization by the destination embassy or Taipei Economic and Cultural Office. The two routes are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: issuance by MOEA -> notarization -> Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular Legalization route: issuance by MOEA -> notarization -> MOEA authentication -> legalization by the destination consular post or Taipei Economic and Cultural Office. Only one authentication path applies to each destination; sequential use of both routes is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors or Incorporator of the Proposed Taiwan Entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: resolution executed before a Taiwan notary public -> notarization -> Apostille by Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular Legalization route: resolution executed before a Taiwan notary public -> notarization -> MOFA authentication -> legalization by the destination jurisdiction's consular office or Taipei Economic and Cultural Office. The selected route must match the status of the destination state and cannot be combined with the other.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All Founding Shareholders and First Directors of the Proposed Taiwan Entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: articles executed before a Taiwan notary public -> notarization -> Apostille by Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular Legalization route: articles executed before a Taiwan notary public -> notarization -> MOFA authentication -> destination consular legalization or Taipei Economic and Cultural Office certification. These alternatives are parallel and mutually exclusive; no successive apostille plus consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Commercial Bank Maintaining the Relevant Account Relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: original letter on bank stationery, officiated by bank manager -> notarization before a Taiwan notary public -> Apostille by Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular Legalization route: original letter on bank stationery, officiated by bank manager -> notarization -> MOFA authentication -> consular legalization by the destination state's consular office or Taipei Economic and Cultural Office. Only one route may be used for a given destination.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified UBO Declaration and Ownership Structure Chart
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporator and Ultimate Beneficial Owners of the Proposed Taiwan Entity, Certified by a Taiwan Notary Public or Certified Public Accountant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: declaration notarized -> Apostille by Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular Legalization route: declaration notarized -> MOFA authentication -> consular legalization by the destination office or Taipei Economic and Cultural Office. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and may not be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every UBO, director, shareholder, licensed person, and registered-agent principal must be screened before filing. Screening shall cover domestic and foreign politically exposed persons as defined by FATF Recommendation 12, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated Lists, the Taiwan consolidated sanctions list, EU restrictive measures, Interpol red notices, adverse media, PEP family members, and close associates. Enhanced due diligence must include source-of-funds verification, independent public-records search, corporate-relationship mapping, and escalated AML compliance officer approval for any hit. All screening results must be documented, time-stamped, and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: MOEA Company Registration Information System and One-Stop Service Portal, Taiwan
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be in Traditional Chinese. An English name may be registered only as a phonetic or translated transliteration of the Chinese legal name, romanised in Mandarin pinyin or in a transliteration appearing in the company constitution. The four-tier naming doctrine is: first, the territorial prefix; second, the distinctive fanciful trade name; third, the statutory business-scope descriptor for company secretarial and registered-agent services; and fourth, the legal-form suffix such as Company Limited or Company Limited by Shares.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant has 15 days from the date of written refusal to file a formal administrative appeal with the MOEA Company Name Review Committee, attaching the refusal decision, the desired name in Traditional Chinese with English transliteration, the four-tier naming structure, a registry search report, and a legal memorandum demonstrating no likelihood of confusion. The MOEA must issue a determination within two months. If the name is rejected again, the applicant may appeal to the Administrative Court under Article 4 of the Administrative Litigation Act of Taiwan.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not per se illegal, but the local tax authority and banks will reject a mere virtual address for this industry because the company secretarial and registered-agent business must maintain an actual physical office with personnel, statutory registers, client files, seals, records, and service-of-process capacity. The National Taxation Administration may reclassify the entity as lacking commercial substance if no operational staff or physical workspace is present, and banks will not open corporate accounts or approve credit-card and bank-wire payment rails for a virtual-office-only registered agent.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: lease or ownership deed, utility invoices, payroll and attendance records, original statutory registers, shareholder register, board minutes, company seal custody log, physical signage, actual staffing, and third-party client files. Quantified risk of unannounced municipal tax or registry inspection is elevated to approximately 45 percent within the first 18 months because this medium-risk AML category holds registered-agent and nominee-type duties and maintains multiple-client UBO files, increasing the likelihood of joint inspections after a suspicious-transaction report or a registered-office change.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Companies Act of 2018 (amended), Articles 1, 2, 6, 8, 9, 18, 98, 101, 128, 129, 161, 172, 192, 202, 208, 218, 235, 278 and 387; read together with the Foreign Investment Act, Articles 4, 6 and 7, and the Regulations on Investment in Taiwan by Foreign or Mainland China Investors.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (Company Registration and One-Stop Service window).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Approval of Incorporation and Registration of a Limited Liability Company under the Taiwan Companies Act, accompanied by the Incorporation Application Form, Articles of Incorporation, and Registration Statement.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None: Taiwan Companies Act does not impose a minimum paid-up capital for a limited liability company; however, the subscribers must fully subscribe and pay for the issued share capital before registration, and the paid-in capital must be verified by a CPA certificate and deposited in a Taiwanese bank escrow-style company capital account pending the issuance of the company registration certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION

The undersigned subscribers and founding incorporators of the Company, acting as the promoters and first board of directors constituted at the incorporation meeting held on [DATE] at [PLACE], do hereby adopt the following resolutions in accordance with the Taiwan Companies Act, the Foreign Investment Act and the Articles of Incorporation executed contemporaneously with this instrument.

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED, that the authorized and issued share capital of the Company be, and it hereby is, fixed at [AMOUNT] New Taiwan Dollars, divided into [NUMBER] shares of par value [PAR VALUE] each, such shares having been fully subscribed and paid for by the foreign investor as evidenced by the capital verification certificate of the certified public accountant and the bank statement of the Company’s designated capital deposit account, and that the board hereby ratifies and confirms the issuance and allotment of such shares to the founding shareholder.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the opening of the Company’s corporate bank accounts at [BANK NAME], Taiwan, is hereby approved, and that the Chairman, the General Manager, and the Chief Financial Officer, acting individually, be and they hereby are authorized, empowered and directed to execute account opening documents, mandates, signature cards, wire transfer instructions and any related agreements, with authority to use the Company seal and to designate authorized signatories whose signatures shall be binding on the Company for all banking purposes.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be, and it hereby is, established at [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS], Taiwan, as the registered office for service of process and statutory notices, and that the directors be authorized to execute the lease, the landlord consent, and the registered office acceptance form and to file the same with the competent registry.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, that [NAME] be and hereby is appointed Chairman of the Board, that [NAME] be and hereby is appointed General Manager, and that [NAME] be and hereby is appointed Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting, with such powers and duties as are prescribed by law and by the Articles of Incorporation, and the Company Secretary is authorized to prepare and submit all statutory filings and registrations to the Ministry of Economic Affairs, the Taxation Administration and other government authorities.

5. WINDOWS AND AGENTS. RESOLVED, that the Company hereby designates [registered agent] as its statutory registered agent in Taiwan with full authority to accept service of process, receive regulatory mail, and maintain the statutory corporate records, and that the directors and officers be authorized to execute any authorization letters or powers of attorney required to implement these resolutions.

This resolution is passed unanimously and shall be effective immediately and continue until amended or revoked by a subsequent resolution of the shareholders or directors lawfully adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Pre-Investment Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC), Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign investor must submit an investment application through the MOEAIC online system setting out the proposed WFOE limited company, the shareholder identities and the business scope classified under ISIC 8299. The application must include certified copies of the investor’s home-country registration, audited financial statements, the proposed Articles of Incorporation and a declaration of the source of funds. The Commission will review the application for negative-list compliance, national security screening and compliance with the Foreign Investment Act. After approval, the investor receives a Foreign Investment Approval Letter, which must be quoted in every subsequent banking and registration filing.
required_dossiers: Foreign investor company registration certificate and apostilled notarial copies
Audited financial statements or solvency declarations for the investing entity
Proposed Articles of Incorporation and business scope statement under ISIC 8299
Power of attorney appointing the local formation agent
Source-of-funds declaration and bank reference letter
Foreign Investment Application Form filed with MOEAIC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the applicant has 30 days to file supplementary materials; if the Commission suspends the application, the formation agent must submit a written response directed to the MOEAIC review committee. In case of a rejection, the investor may apply for administrative reconsideration under the Administrative Appeal Act within 30 days of receiving the written dismissal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval Online System)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The applicant must reserve the proposed company name and confirm that the business scope of company secretarial and registered agent services is permissible for a wholly foreign-owned enterprise. The online name pre-approval application must state the exact Chinese and English names of the company and list the intended ISIC 8299 activities, including corporate secretarial maintenance, registered agent services, offshore company administration and statutory filing support. No duplication with an existing company name is allowed, and the proposed name must not be misleading or contrary to public policy. Upon issuance, the name reservation is valid for six months and must be included in the incorporation application dossier.
required_dossiers: Company Name Reservation Application Form
Business scope description in English corresponding to ISIC 8299
Foreign Investment Approval Letter or pending investment reference number
Identity or incorporation certificate of the founding shareholder
Applicant’s authorization letter to the resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, the applicant may submit a new name application the same day without an appeal fee. If the rejection rests on business scope incompatibility, the applicant must file a written objection with the Department of Commerce and provide authority under the Companies Act for the proposed service activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Escrow Capital Account and Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated commercial bank in Taiwan (for example, a branch of Bank of Taiwan or Cathay United Bank) and the certified public accountant appointed by the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Foreign Investment Approval and the name reservation, the resident agent must open a company capital account in the name of the WFOE Limited Company at a licensed Taiwanese bank. The foreign shareholder must wire the full subscribed capital into the designated blocked capital account, and the bank must issue a capital remittance certificate evidencing the inward remittance. The appointed CPA must then prepare a capital verification report confirming that the capital is fully paid, unencumbered, and available for company use only after the Ministry of Economic Affairs issues the registration certificate. The CPA report, together with the bank certificate, becomes part of the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Company name reservation certificate
Articles of Incorporation draft
Bank account opening documents and resolution of the subscriber
Capital remittance inward report from the foreign shareholder’s bank
CPA capital verification report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank flags the remittance as a suspicious transaction, the investor must provide source-of-funds documentation to the bank’s AML unit and notify the Ministry of Economic Affairs. If the CPA refuses to certify the capital, the company must remedy any incomplete payment or legal defect in the shareholder subscription and redeposit funds before resubmitting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation and Statutory Registration with MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (Company Registration Division)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The formation agent must file the incorporation application with the MOEA one-stop company registration window, attaching the stamped Articles of Incorporation, the foreign investment approval, the name reservation, the CPA verification certificate, the registered office consent, and the director and officer acceptance forms. The filing may be submitted electronically with a qualified signature of the resident agent. The registry will examine the compliance of the legal capital, the lawful business scope and the appointment of statutory officers. Upon approval, the MOEA issues the Company Registration Certificate, which is the conclusive evidence of incorporation and grant of legal personality. The company must then obtain its company seal and register the seal specimen with the registry if required.
required_dossiers: Incorporation application form
Stamp-tax paid Articles of Incorporation
Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Name reservation certificate
CPA capital verification certificate and bank remittance certificate
Registered office lease and landlord consent
Directors’ and officers’ ID copies and acceptance letters
Company seal specimen form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a notice of deficiency, the applicant may cure within 15 days under Article 388 of the Companies Act. If the registration is suspended due to doubts over shareholder eligibility or capital verification, the company may submit a written clarification, and if the administrative decision is adverse, the company may pursue administrative appeal within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Labor Registration, and Post-Incorporation Ancillary Permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance; Bureau of Labor Insurance; local fire department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following incorporation, the company must complete tax registration with the National Taxation Bureau to obtain the Unified Business Number and the tax registration certificate. The registration form must state the nature of the secretarial and registered agent services for VAT and profit-seeking enterprise tax purposes. The company must also register as an employer with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and the National Health Insurance Administration for social insurance compliance. If the company will use an office, the local fire department must inspect the premises and issue a fire safety certificate. Any renewal of the registered agent license will be handled by the company secretary through the MOEA online system.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Unified Business Number application form and company seal specimen
Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Employment, labor insurance and health insurance registration forms for initial officers
Office fire safety inspection request and floor plan
Identity documents of directors and controllers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority delays issuance of the Unified Business Number, the company may operate provisionally under the pending number and cure after verification. For labor registration errors, the company may file a correction application retroactive to the first day of employment. Fire department refusal can be cured by installing the required alarm and suppression equipment and scheduling a re-inspection within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs; local municipal government commercial registry for the physical office address
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Registration Certificate and Company Registration Certificate; no separate industrial operating license is required for a corporate secretarial and registered agent service office classified under ISIC 8299.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan (Taiwan EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable — pure administrative, commercial registered agent and corporate secretarial services; no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing activity within ISIC 8299.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no wastewater discharge points, VOC emission sources, or hazardous waste generation. If the office later installs backup generators or substantial electronic equipment, the company must comply with stationary emission source permitting thresholds under the Air Pollution Control Act and register electronic waste handling with the Taiwan EPA if annual waste volume exceeds regulatory exemptions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable at the heavy-industrial level; for the administrative office, the local fire department must certify the fire safety inspection and exit routes under the Fire Services Act. The premises must meet the structural load requirements of the Building Act for office occupancy, and the company must complete occupational hazard notification only if it employs more than 300 workers; otherwise, a simple self-assessment under the Occupational Safety and Health Act is sufficient.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, exercised through local STA service bureaus; online electronic tax filing is administered via the STA Electronic Tax Bureau portal (etax.chinatax.gov.cn).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign investors establishing the WFOE must first complete enterprise registration with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). Upon issuance of the Business License, the WFOE receives an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is also the taxpayer identification number for tax purposes. The USCC is automatically shared with the STA through the multi-department 'one-stop' registration integration, so no separate tax registration application is required. Within the statutory post-incorporation period, the WFOE must use the STA Electronic Tax Bureau to complete legal representative biometric real-name verification, financial accounting system filing, bank account reporting, VAT taxpayer status election (small-scale taxpayer or general taxpayer), and, where cross-border services are contemplated, registration for cross-border zero-rating or VAT exemption status. A foreign non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment that earns China-source income obtains a non-resident enterprise tax registration through its appointed withholding agent or through the STA Electronic Tax Bureau non-resident registration module, and receives a separate tax reference number for withholding compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - the People's Republic of China does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election or a separate hybrid mismatch elective regime for a WFOE; the entity is a Chinese resident enterprise taxed at entity level. Thin capitalization, controlled foreign corporation rules, and general anti-avoidance rules apply as non-elective statutory provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for VAT registration; all Chinese enterprises are mandatorily registered upon incorporation. General taxpayer status is mandatory when annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000, while taxpayers below that threshold may elect small-scale taxpayer simplified taxation subject to STA rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered entities must issue invoices through the State Taxation Administration-approved e-invoice platform using the unified electronic invoice system. Full digital electronic invoices are transmitted to the STA in real time; the platform performs automated anti-fraud checks including unique invoice number allocation, buyer-seller master data matching, tax control UKey digital signature validation, and cross-reference with VAT returns, customs declarations, and bank receipts under the Golden Tax Phase IV system. There is no conventional physical 'pre-clearance stamp' requirement; instead, the digital platform performs real-time clearance and risk blocking before the invoice can be legally considered valid.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for (a) goods physically exported from China under customs supervision where title passes to an overseas buyer and the goods leave the customs territory; and (b) cross-border taxable services supplied to wholly overseas recipients that fall within the STA-approved zero-rated or VAT-exempt cross-border services scope, including qualifying offshore business and secretarial services, provided the service recipient is outside China, the service is consumed outside China, and payment is received in foreign currency. All zero-rated claims require contemporaneous documentation proving the export or offshore supply nature of the transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Customs Export Goods Declaration) with approved customs release information
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) showing the exporter, overseas consignee, and port of discharge/customs exit
Full set of commercial invoices and packing lists matching the customs declaration
Export sales contract or purchase order identifying the overseas buyer and contract terms
Bank foreign exchange collection voucher or inward remittance receipt issued by a SAFE-designated bank evidencing FX inflow
VAT invoice issued in accordance with export VAT zero-rating rules (if any)
Electronic export tax rebate application/supporting log filed through the STA Electronic Tax Bureau
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and customs jointly scrutinize zero-rating claims. If the customs export declaration, transport documentation, or foreign exchange receipt is false, incomplete, or inconsistent, or if the foreign exchange proceeds are not repatriated within the mandatory deadline unless validly extended, the zero-rating is retrospectively revoked, VAT becomes payable with daily late surcharge of 0.05%, and a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax may be imposed under Articles 63 and 64 of the Law on Tax Administration and Collection. Fraudulently obtaining an export VAT refund additionally exposes the entity and its responsible persons to criminal liability under Article 204 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, and the export tax refund registration status may be suspended.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBOC), acting through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The PRC maintains a managed floating exchange rate regime with strict capital account controls and current account convertibility for genuine trade and service transactions. For the Taiwan-invested WFOE, registered capital injections from the Taiwan shareholder are capital account transactions: they require FDI foreign exchange registration, a domestic foreign exchange capital account, and SAFE-monitored use, and the proceeds cannot be diverted to equity investment, entrusted lending, securities, or real estate unless expressly permitted. Current account items, such as cross-border fee payments for company secretarial services, are generally convertible at market rates once the bank validates the underlying contract, invoice, tax payment status, and beneficial ownership. Profit remittance to the Taiwan parent is permitted after the annual audit, final tax settlement, and board profit distribution resolution, with bank review of the audited financial statements, tax clearance certificate, and historical capital verification report. The convertibility assessment is therefore qualified: operational payments are freely routable, but all capital movements remain subject to SAFE registration, quota controls, bank confirmation, and genuine transaction documentation. There is no full liberalization of cross-border RMB or foreign currency flows, and any attempt to use offshore digital EMI accounts to bypass SAFE reporting would be unlawful.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export-related foreign currency receipts must be repatriated to the domestic foreign exchange settlement account of the WFOE within 180 days after customs declaration; there is no fixed statutory conversion ratio, but the bank will verify the export value against customs records, and any conversion to RMB or retention in foreign currency must be reported under SAFE's current account receipt management system. Proceeds must be surrendered through a tier-1 domestic bank using the correct export verification code.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low or prohibitive. The PBOC and SAFE license regime does not authorize offshore fintech EMIs to maintain deposit accounts, process capital account transactions, or clear RMB and foreign exchange for PRC-domiciled entities. Licensed domestic non-bank payment institutions (Alipay, WeChat Pay, and SAFE-registered cross-border payment institutions) may only handle qualifying current account e-commerce or consumer payments and cannot replace a tier-1 bank for corporate treasury. Use of offshore EMI rails for corporate collections would create an AML gap and violate SAFE data reporting. Hence the WFOE must rely on onshore tier-1 banks; fintech EMI rails may be used at most as a front-end invoicing or collection gateway in a fully disclosed and segregated structure, never as the primary clearing mechanism.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under PBOC anti-money-laundering and account verification rules, the legal representative or an authorized senior officer must normally attend an in-branch face-to-face interview for first-time account opening. If the legal representative is non-resident or cannot travel, the bank may accept a notarized power of attorney executed in Taiwan, legalized and translated, together with the physical presence of the authorized person in mainland China; remote consular proxy opening without any physical attendance is generally not accepted by tier-1 state banks. Banks may require the Taiwan shareholder's certificate of incorporation, director resolution, and UBO declarations to be notarized, legalized, and translated into English and Chinese before the interview is approved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque ownership chain: Taiwan corporate shareholder is itself held through offshore nominee layers and the registered agent business creates possible shell-company facilitation risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Incumbency for each layer in the ownership chain; register of directors and shareholders; UBO declaration with full civil identity data; audited financial statements of the immediate Taiwan shareholder for the last two years; bank reference letters from Taiwan banks; notarized and legalized resolutions; articles of association; certificate of good standing; capital source and asset provenance evidence for the registered capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business-scope mismatch and enhanced medium-risk classification for ISIC 8299 company secretarial activities; the bank may suspect nominee-services, no real operational substance, or facilitation of third-party entities tax evasion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PRC business license and the statutory license or filing for registered agent and secretarial services; lease agreement for physical office; payroll and social insurance records of employees; organization chart; detailed client service contracts and deliverables such as board minutes, statutory notices, and filing records; itemized invoices and tax payment certificates; one-year business plan; internal policies for client onboarding, AML screening, and refusal of nominee shareholder structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from Taiwan parent into a capital account with no clear foreign-exchange purpose code or no evidence that paid-in capital can be traced to legitimate operating surplus; bank risk of structuring or placement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) registration or foreign exchange information filing receipt; the foreign investor's bank credit reference; board resolution authorizing the capital injection; subscription agreement; capital verification report issued by a licensed CPA after funds arrival; source-of-funds bank statements for the remitting account; tax compliance declaration in Taiwan; and an undertaking to use funds solely for the registered business within the negative-list limits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound service fee remittances, such as offshore secretarial or registered agent fees paid to Taiwan affiliates, that look like profit stripping or invoice fraud with insufficient service documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: For each remittance: executed service agreement with deliverables and timeline; commercial invoices; Chinese official tax invoices; proof of actual delivery such as electronic or physical filings, meeting minutes, email logs, and registered office service orders; withholding tax and enterprise income tax payment receipts; SAFE current-account transaction registration; letter confirming the counterparty is not a shell; beneficial ownership declarations; and an annual transfer-pricing documentation file satisfying the independent-transaction standard.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan-resident investor must complete SAFE FDI basic registration and open a foreign exchange capital account at a tier-1 domestic bank before remitting. The remitter must use SWIFT MT103 with a precise FDI investment purpose code naming the WFOE as beneficiary and attaching notarized incorporation documents of the Taiwan investor. Upon crediting, the bank verifies the payment against SAFE records, issues a capital item receipt confirmation, and a licensed CPA performs capital verification. Funds may subsequently be converted to RMB only for permitted operating purposes, with explicit prohibitions on equity investment, entrusted loans, real estate other than self-use, and securities speculation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For goods-trade settlements, the WFOE may use commercial letters of credit and documentary collections routed through a Chinese advising or confirming bank. For service-trade payments, including company secretarial and registered agent fees, the standard clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 through the tier-1 bank's international settlement department, with CIPS for cross-border RMB. The bank classifies the entity under SAFE trade verification; A-class enterprises can process standard payments with contracts, invoices, tax withholding evidence, and purpose codes, while B or C-class enterprises require pre-approval and enhanced scanning. High-value payments are subject to PBOC large-sum transaction reporting and sanctions-name screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB and foreign-currency forward contracts, limited to real trade or investment exposure and approved current or capital account positions
FX swaps between RMB and foreign currency for short-term liquidity mismatches, with compulsory SAFE reporting and bank confirmation of underlying exposure
Cross-currency swaps for long-term capital and dividend exposure, permissible when registered and backed by genuine cross-border investment or debt flows
Plain-vanilla foreign-currency options used for hedging only, permitted by licensed banks under SAFE real-demand rules; speculative, leveraged, or layered options are prohibited

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for onshore PRC corporate accounts; a PRC WFOE cannot book RMB NDFs domestically, and offshore NDFs cannot be used to settle or hedge PRC-sourced treasury obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders Meeting (AGM) minutes and audited / board-approved financial statements, business report, and profit appropriation proposal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must convene by June 30 for calendar-year entities; minutes and financial statements must be filed with MOEA within 15 days after the AGM (final filing date July 15 at the latest)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible director fined NT$10,000 to NT$50,000 per violation per Article 383 of the Company Act; continuing non-compliance allows MOEA to order rectification, impose repeated fines, and ultimately initiate administrative strike-off / compulsory dissolution of the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-seeking Enterprise Income Tax settlement return and final tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, R.O.C. (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar year: filing and full payment due by May 31 of the following year (noon deadline); one additional month for filing only is permitted for companies engaged a licensed tax agent, but full tax payment is still due by May 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing within two months: 3% extra tax on unpaid amount; after two months: 5% extra tax; interest accrues daily at the Bank of Taiwan postal savings one-year deposit rate until payment; deliberate tax evasion attracts a penalty of 20% to 32% of understated tax plus criminal liability for responsible officers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quarterly Business Tax (VAT) return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, R.O.C. (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly calendar periods; due by the 15th day of the month following the quarter end (January 15, April 15, July 15, October 15)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If no overdue tax but return filed late: fine of NT$1,500 to NT$15,000; if there is overdue tax: additional penalty equal to 15% of the understated VAT amount plus daily interest at statutory late-payment rate; repeat violations can trigger business suspension for up to two weeks and administrative strike-off of the registered office license

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Operation Report for the wholly foreign-owned enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 for the preceding calendar year; for newly approved investments, initial report due within 30 days after fiscal year end; any capital or shareholding change must be filed within 30 days of the transaction closing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit exposes the WFOE to fines of NT$10,000 to NT$50,000 per event and possible revocation of the foreign investment approval, forced share repatriation, and loss of tax treaty benefits; persistent default may result in administrative deregistration of the investment license

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT annual compliance report and independent audit for the company secretarial and registered-agent DNFBP operation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) and the Money Laundering Control Act compliance unit, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Internal AML/CFT risk assessment and annual independent audit must be completed by December 31 of each calendar year, approved by the board, and filed with the FIU within 30 days after board adoption (typically by March 31 of the next year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance fines from NT$50,000 to NT$2,500,000 under Article 32 of the Money Laundering Control Act; aggravated or repeat violations can lead to revocation of the registered agent license, director disqualification, and administrative strike-off from the company secretarial registry

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO register update and annual confirmation of shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and share transfer records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, MOEA and Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any transfer of shares or change of UBO must be filed with MOEA within 30 days of the occurrence; annual confirmation of the full shareholder and UBO list is submitted together with the annual financial statements by June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing after the 30-day window: NT$10,000 to NT$50,000 fine per incident and parallel FIU administrative penalties; deliberate concealment of UBO information is a criminal offense punishable by up to two years imprisonment and corporate fine up to NT$10,000,000; persistent non-compliance for two consecutive annual cycles triggers administrative strike-off of the company registration

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent certified public accountant (CPA) audit required for: (i) any Taiwan-incorporated company, including WFOE, with paid-in capital exceeding NT$30,000,000; (ii) any company whose annual turnover exceeds NT$300,000,000; (iii) financial institutions, insurance undertakings, and public companies; (iv) companies that are part of a consolidated tax filing group or that receive foreign investment approval requiring audited statements; and (v) registered-agent / company secretarial entities designated as non-financial businesses and professions (DNFBPs) with a medium-risk or higher AML classification, where the FSC or FIU may mandate a CPA audit irrespective of size. Below these thresholds, financial statements must still be prepared in accordance with applicable accounting standards but may remain unaudited unless the company seeks bank credit above NT$50,000,000 or is otherwise ordered by the competent authority.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan International Financial Reporting Standards (TW-IFRS) for companies that meet the compulsory audit threshold or are listed / regulated; the Enterprise Accounting Standard (EAS) for small and medium enterprises not exceeding the statutory audit thresholds; all financial statements must be reconciled with the profit-seeking enterprise income tax return filed with the Ministry of Finance.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not require a standalone annual UBO filing to a separate registry, but the company must (i) maintain an updated UBO register at all times; (ii) report any share transfer or change of beneficial ownership to the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 calendar days of the transaction; and (iii) submit an annual confirmation of the UBO register and shareholder list together with the annual financial statements at the AGM, which must be filed with MOEA by no later than June 30 of the following fiscal year. Failure to observe the 30-day reporting window carries separate contempt fines and may invalidate the transfer with respect to the company.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders and Directors

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 – USD 3,000 per year for professional registered office and corporate secretarial agent services in Taipei / Taiwan major cities
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – USD 12,000 per year for a WFOE that meets the mandatory CPA audit threshold, depending on transaction volume, group complexity, and service provider tier

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified Small and Low-Profit Enterprises enjoy a 20% statutory reduced rate and, under the current preferential calculation, taxable income up to RMB 3 million is included at 25% before tax is applied at 20%, yielding an effective 5% rate. A qualifying Hainan Free Trade Port encouraged industry or a High-New Technology Enterprise may use a 15% rate; certain Western Region encouraged industries also qualify for 15%. China does not operate a traditional patent box, but it grants a 100% extra super deduction for qualifying R&D expenditures, allowing an effective 200% deduction. For an ISIC 8299 registered-agent and offshore secretarial WFOE, the standard headline CIT rate is 25% absent a special regional or industry certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, A-Class) together with supplementary schedules A105000, A105050, A105080 and related-party transaction declaration forms, all filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration Electronic Taxpayer (E-Tax) Portal by the WFOE legal representative or appointed tax filing agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement with quarterly provisional prepayments; quarterly instalment returns and payments are due through the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual A100000 return and final CIT settlement must be filed within five months after the close of the fiscal year, normally 31 May for a calendar-year WFOE. Quarterly provisional CIT prepayments must be filed and paid within 15 days after the end of each quarter. Dividend withholding tax on outbound distributions must be remitted within 15 days after the end of the month in which the distribution is declared.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit (total profit) as reported in the PRC financial statements before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must prepare accounts under PRC GAAP. Payments to the Taiwan parent for management fees, secretarial support or offshore agent services cannot reduce accounting profit unless supported by genuine contracts, invoices, evidence of actual service and service-receipt records; otherwise they are added back in Box 2.

All cross-border disbursements lacking arm's length substance must be added back: inflated related-party interest, unsupported royalties, entertainment expenses exceeding the statutory caps, corporate secretarial fees paid to a shell affiliate without economic benefit, and transfer-pricing differences determined by the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income decrease adjustments (deductions and exemptions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accelerated depreciation lawfully claimed, qualifying R&D super deductions, and incentive incomes supported by statutory certificates may be subtracted. A WFOE may not unilaterally reduce taxable income by treating dividends declared but unpaid to a Taiwan shareholder as a deductible expense.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after permanent and temporary differences (Line 1 + Line 2 - Line 3).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border groups must align this line with the arm's length profit determination. If an Advance Pricing Agreement has been reached, the adjusted arm's length result is the relevant figure. Non-resident parent entities cannot substitute their own determination without contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax rate for computing CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert 25% for the standard non-preferential case. A 15% rate is allowed only if the WFOE holds a valid certificate or free-zone registration; the absence of a certificate makes the 25% headline rate compulsory. The Taiwan shareholder's DTA status does not change the WFOE-level CIT rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed income tax equals taxable income multiplied by the rate in Line 5.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This amount is the WFOE's entity-level CIT. Inbound investors must distinguish this tax from dividend WHT, which is a separate non-resident tax imposed on the shareholder, not on the WFOE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reductions and exemptions claimed in the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only claim statutory reductions such as small-low-profit, high-tech enterprise, Hainan free-zone or Western Region incentives with documentary proof. A registered-agent/service business cannot rely on manufacturing-oriented tax holidays.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit for taxes paid abroad on foreign-source income already included in the WFOE's accounting profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE itself receives foreign-source income, the credit is capped at the amount of PRC CIT allocable to that foreign-source income. A Taiwan parent's foreign tax is never credited against the WFOE's tax, and a refund or treaty relief at shareholder level is separate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Actual CIT payable after reducing Line 6 by Line 7 and Line 8.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE contractually agreed to bear the Taiwan shareholder's withholding tax on grossed-up dividends or fees, that gross-up itself is a deemed income or distribution requiring further CIT and WHT treatment; ignoring this triggers a hidden tax liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT already prepaid through quarterly provisional instalments during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all quarterly prepayments made within 15 days of each quarter-end. Underpayment of instalments creates daily 0.05% late surcharges from the moment each instalment becomes due. A WFOE that made no provisional payments must not offset the annual balance without penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final CIT balance due or refundable for the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the final balance by 31 May. For a WFOE that has distributed or intends to distribute dividends to a Taiwan parent, the dividend WHT must be independently withheld and paid at the time of distribution; the tax authority can pursue unpaid withholding from the WFOE as the withholding agent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing of Form A100000 attracts a fine under Article 62 of the Tax Collection Administration Law of up to RMB 2,000, and from RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 in serious cases. Unpaid or underpaid CIT additionally attracts a daily 0.05% overdue surcharge under Article 32. Intentional concealment or false filing constitutes tax evasion under Article 63, exposing the taxpayer to recovery of the tax plus a penalty of 50% to 5 times the underpaid amount. Criminal fraud thresholds under Criminal Law Article 201 are met when the evaded tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and represents more than 10% of the total taxable amount; a serious amount with a ratio exceeding 30% carries imprisonment from 3 up to 7 years, plus fines. The legal representative and responsible tax director risk a tax-dishonesty blacklist, travel bans and exit restriction orders for unpaid taxes.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends paid by the PRC WFOE to a non-resident corporate shareholder under Articles 3, 37 and 38 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law; the rate may be reduced to 5% under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement if the Taiwan-resident beneficial owner directly holds at least 25% of the WFOE's capital and such ownership is maintained for the period required by the agreement, provided no mainland permanent establishment is attributable to the shareholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Under SAT Announcement [2019] No. 35, the Taiwan-resident beneficial owner or the WFOE withholding agent must electronically submit a treaty-benefit filing, attaching a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the competent Taiwan tax authority, a beneficial ownership declaration, the shareholder register and constitutional documents, audited financial evidence of substance, and supporting documentation that the Taiwan entity is not a mere conduit. The WFOE, as withholding agent, must apply the reduced treaty rate at source only after such documentation is received; withhold the domestic 10% if documentation is incomplete, and preserve all records for at least 10 years. If treaty relief is denied, the WFOE must remit the full 10% and the shareholder may pursue a MAP or refund under the cross-strait mechanism.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory PRC rates on outbound interest and royalties are both 10% on the gross amount paid to a non-resident enterprise, plus applicable VAT and surtaxes on the underlying service. Under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement, interest is eligible for a reduced 7% rate and royalties for a 10% treaty rate when the Taiwan resident is the beneficial owner of the interest or rights and has no mainland permanent establishment to which the income is effectively connected. For non-Treaty offshore jurisdictions, the statutory 10% rate applies to both categories of passive income.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File preparation is mandatory when, in a single fiscal year, related-party tangible property transfers reach RMB 200 million, financial asset transfers reach RMB 100 million, intangible asset transfers reach RMB 100 million, or related-party service transactions reach RMB 40 million. Master File preparation is mandatory when aggregate related-party transactions reach RMB 1 billion in a fiscal year. The WFOE must also disclose the existence and amount of each related-party transaction in the annual CIT return schedules whenever any reportable related-party dealing is present.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The PRC does not impose a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation regime, but economic substance is decisive through the tax treaties' beneficial ownership requirement, Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law general anti-abuse rule, and the permanent establishment tests. A WFOE performing ISIC 8299 registered-agent and offshore secretarial services must demonstrate real offices, locally employed staff, decision-making files, board minutes, client contracts, Chinese compliance records, and invoicing functions. If the WFOE or its Taiwan parent is a mailbox shell and profits are shifted without core income-generating activities in mainland China, the tax authority may recharacterize the arrangement, deny treaty benefits, impute taxable profits and impose 10% WHT on deemed distributions or royalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Unfiled or Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE's directors sign and submit Form A100000 that omits fee income earned from offshore secretarial and registered-agent services, fabricates expense invoices from shell service companies, misclassifies distributions to non-resident shareholders as consulting fees, or deliberately understates taxable revenue to reduce CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law, the tax authority recovers the underpaid tax and imposes a penalty of 50% to 5 times the evaded amount, with daily 0.05% late surcharge. Criminal Law Article 201 criminalizes tax evasion where the amount evaded exceeds RMB 50,000 and exceeds 10% of total taxable amount; imprisonment of up to 3 years applies for the ordinary threshold, and 3 to 7 years for large amounts with a ratio above 30%, plus fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who ordered, concealed or signed the false return is a directly responsible person under Chinese criminal law and may be sentenced to imprisonment and fines. If personal and company assets are commingled or the corporate form is abused to evade tax debts, courts may pierce the corporate veil under Company Law Article 20 and hold the director personally liable for the tax liabilities, penalties and civil restitution. The responsible legal representative also faces a tax-dishonesty public blacklist and exit restriction order banning cross-border travel.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Fraudulent Claim of Cross-Strait DTA Relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE and a Taiwan-resident mailbox holding company file false beneficial ownership papers to claim the 5% reduced dividend WHT when the ultimate owner is a PRC resident or a Hong Kong intermediary; the Taiwanese entity has no employees, offices or business control, and the WFOE routes dividend payments through that synthetic shell to obtain treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority invokes Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and its implementing general anti-abuse rules to recharacterize the income, deny the treaty benefit, re-collect the full 10% WHT, impose daily surcharges, and apply a 50% to 5 times penalty under Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law. False statements to the tax authority in treaty documentation can trigger criminal liability under Article 201 or Article 204 of the Criminal Law, with penal regimes extending to fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute false treaty declarations or approve dividends without verifying the Taiwan beneficial owner's substance are personally exposed: the tax authority can attribute civil restitution for the under-withheld tax, the travel ban blacklist will apply to the legal representative, and criminal prosecution can lead to imprisonment of up to 7 years. Where the WFOE is found to be a pure conduit, the corporate veil can be pierced and director assets attached.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Default and Profit Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE fails to prepare contemporaneous Local File or Master File despite exceeding the statutory thresholds, books related-party secretarial fees to the Taiwan parent at an arbitrary margin, pays annual management fees without evidence of real service, or misleadingly completes the related-party transaction schedules in the annual CIT return to hide intercompany flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 41 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and SAT Announcement [2016] No. 42, the tax authority may apply the CUP, TNMM or Profit Split method to adjust taxable income upward. Failure to produce documentation on demand after the statutory deadline attracts a fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 100,000 under Article 44 of the Tax Collection Administration Law, plus daily 0.05% surcharges on the additional tax. If the omission is fraudulent and designed to evade tax, Articles 62 and 63 elevate the consequence to recovery, a 50% to 5 times penalty, and criminal liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer-pricing documentation or who deliberately shift profits to a low-tax shell are personally liable if the WFOE becomes unable to pay the adjusted CIT and penalties; the personal accounts of directors may be frozen, and the tax authority may impose travel bans and exit restrictions. In aggravated tax evasion cases, the director qualifies as a directly responsible person subject to criminal conviction, with imprisonment up to 7 years and financial penalties.
